title: Runtime Debt Playbook and Remediation Roster
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Summary:
This playbook centralizes identification, scoring, and remediation of persistent technical debt affecting the serving runtime. It is intended to be actionable: each roster item contains an owner, reproducible test, remediation steps, CI/observability gates, and verification criteria. Use this document as the single source for planning debt sprints and for informing SRE/incident prioritization.

Audience and scope:
- Audience: runtime engineers, SREs, program managers, and product owners who approve runtime changes.
- Scope: core runtime components (dispatcher, scheduler-agent, kernel-coordinator, slot-synth, kv-cache shards, observer-collector). Excludes client SDKs, documentation debt outside runtime, and infra account billing items.

Taxonomy and risk model:
- Taxonomy: Code debt, Test/CI debt, Observability debt, Operational process debt, Data/migration debt.
- Risk model: compute a numeric score (1-25) = Severity x Exposure x Reproducibility, where each factor is 1-5.
  - Severity: SLO impact if left unresolved (1 low - 5 catastrophic).
  - Exposure: percent of traffic or customers affected (1 <1% - 5 >50%).
  - Reproducibility: how easy it is to trigger in test (1 hard - 5 trivial).
- Priority bands: Low 1-6, Medium 7-12, High 13-18, Critical 19-25.

Remediation lifecycle (required for every roster item):
1) Triage: Owner documents symptoms, evidence, and a minimal reproducible case.
2) Scoring: Owner assigns Severity, Exposure, Reproducibility and computes score.
3) Plan: Author a remediation plan with an estimate (Quick, Small, Medium, Large), rollback plan, and validation checklist.
4) PR & CI: Changes must include unit tests, an integration test where feasible, and a CI job tag referencing this roster item.
5) Shadow & Canary: For High/Critical items, run 24-72h shadow traffic followed by staged canary rollouts (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with automated rollback criteria.
6) Close: Owner posts retrospective, updates the roster status to Resolved, and records measured SLO/cost impact.

Verification and gating requirements (minimum):
- Unit and integration coverage for modified code paths.
- New or extended metrics and an alert (metric, baseline, threshold, window).
- A synthetic reproducible harness entry in the benchmarking suite for items that affect latency or throughput.
- Post-deploy check: 72h shadow or mirrored run for High/Critical items, compare p50/p95/p99 and cost per token to baseline.

Remediation roster (examples):
- ID: ROSTER-101
  Title: Asymmetric kvcache invalidation after point-upgrade
  Component: kv-cache shards
  Owner: Lena Zhou
  Created: 2025-01-15
  Status: open
  Risk score: 17
  Symptoms: Some shard nodes show kvcache_miss_spike after staggered kafka replays; affected routes show p99 increases for 30-90 minutes.
  Repro steps: Controlled rolling upgrade on staging with staggered restart and synthetic multi-turn traces.
  Remediation plan: Stabilize invalidation protocol, persist prefetch hints, and add a graceful drain handshake between dispatcher and shard.
  CI gates: Integration test simulating staggered restarts; metric kvcache_hit_rate must not drop >10% in test.
  Validation: 48h shadow and a 3-stage canary.

- ID: ROSTER-112
  Title: Priority inversion under mixed short/long requests
  Component: scheduler-agent
  Owner: Ravi Patel
  Created: 2025-06-02
  Status: in_progress
  Risk score: 20
  Symptoms: Under sustained mixed traffic, low-latency workload p99 balloons due to long-running batches delaying preemption.
  Repro steps: Mixed-workload harness that sends 1:5 ratio of short:long requests at sustained qps.
  Remediation plan: Implement preemptive batch slicing and a credit rebalancer; introduce backpressure signals from kernel-coordinator.
  CI gates: New scheduler simulator regression tests, end-to-end latency lab.
  Validation: Shadow two production routes for 72h, expect p99 reduction >30% for short requests.

- ID: ROSTER-123
  Title: Kernel plugin lifecycle leak (third-party accelerators)
  Component: kernel-coordinator
  Owner: Marco Delgado
  Created: 2025-08-10
  Status: backlog
  Risk score: 12
  Symptoms: Memory growth on nodes using experimental accelerator plugin after repeated model loads.
  Repro steps: Repeated model load/unload loop on testbed with mixed quantization variants.
  Remediation plan: Add reference counting to plugin lifecycle and defensive cleanup paths; add integration test in plugin sandbox.
  CI gates: Plugin sandbox memory regression test.
  Validation: No growth over 48h soak in canary.

- ID: ROSTER-137
  Title: Dispatcher GRPC channel reuse policy causes short-lived connection thrash
  Component: dispatcher
  Owner: Ava Martinez
  Created: 2025-11-01
  Status: open
  Risk score: 14
  Symptoms: Connection churn and brief spikes in CPU during microbursts.
  Repro steps: Burst traffic harness and connection churn monitor.
  Remediation plan: Implement connection pooling and tuned keepalive/backoff; add stress test to burst harness.
  CI gates: Stress test with connection churn metric reduced by >= 70%.
  Validation: Canary with burst simulation in production shadow channel.

Operational playbook for items that cause incidents:
- Immediate action: If a roster item is implicated in an SLO breach or incident, mark it P0 and trigger an incident review; assign a short remediation runway (hotfix or mitigation) with an SRE owner.
- Communication: Notify Customer Success and affected customers within the incident timeline if the issue is user-visible.
- Follow up: Add remediation item to next sprint and track completion in retrospective.

Dashboards and queries (examples to copy into Grafana/BigQuery):
- kvcache_hit_rate_by_shard: SELECT shard, avg(kvcache_hit) FROM runtime_metrics WHERE job='kvcache' AND time > now() - 1h GROUP BY shard
- scheduler_pending_credit_balance: derive credit imbalance and alert when > 80th percentile for 10m.
- connection_churn_rate: rate(grpc_conn_create_total[1m]) by dispatcher_zone

Quarterly KPIs and reporting:
- Publish a quarterly debt report with: open items by priority band, average time to remediation, observed SLO improvement post-remediation, estimated cost delta.
- Target: reduce Critical items by 40% QoQ until Critical <= 3.

Templates and checklist (copy into Jira ticket or PR):
- Summary, Repro steps, Benchmark harness name, Risk score, Remediation steps, Validation checklist (unit/integration/shadow/canary), Rollback criteria, Observability changes (metrics/alerts), Related runbooks, Owner.

Appendix: example rollback criteria (must be machine-readable in deploy system):
- If p99 latency on route X > baseline * 1.5 for 10m, rollback.
- If kvcache_hit_rate drops > 15% for 30m after change, rollback.
